To find \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x)\), look at the graph as \(x\) approaches \(2\) from the right side (values greater than \(2\)).

For \(x>2\), the graph is the slanted line that begins at the open circle \((2,4)\). As \(x\) approaches \(2\) from the right, the corresponding \(y\)-values approach \(4\). The open circle means \(f(2)\neq 4\), but limits depend on nearby values, not the value at \(x=2\).

Therefore,
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 2^+} f(x)=4}
\]
